title: Calcium–albumin coupling gives no clear incremental inflammation prediction across two NHANES surveys
abstract: We tested whether a centered total-calcium-by-albumin interaction predicts concurrent CRP>3 mg/L beyond separate nonlinear chemistry and routine physiological predictors. A survey-weighted logistic model was fitted in 14,403 NHANES III adults and frozen for 4,596 separately recruited 2017–2018 adults. Adding the interaction changed weighted Brier score by -0.00001392 (approximate fixed-fit target-PSU bootstrap 95% interval -0.00005667 to 0.00002981) and AUC by 0.00013163. The interval crosses zero; discovery out-of-fold Brier worsened, and an additive-spline comparator showed essentially no gain. Joint training/target uncertainty also crossed zero. This narrowly scoped inconclusive result does not support a practically useful increment for the tested representation, and does not measure ionized calcium or establish absent biological coupling.
